judgements.justification: A's Reviewer_A5qv doubted the conceptual gain on the wrong claim that a d^2 SQ bound follows from DKS17 (the paper credits DKS19, which does not transfer); no B reviewer made that error.
Both spotlights match ratings of 7 and 8 with no dissent, and A's Reviewer_9D9p proposed a spotlight; no chair went above the reviewers.
Each committee has one thin 8 (8XsW in A, LQDD in B), both at confidence 4; the feature is symmetric and explains no divergence.
The authors sent both committees the same text on the SoS caveat; no flaw was disclosed to one committee only.
Both committees treated the shared SoS-versus-SQ caveat as framing in the same way; neither discounted a flaw the other weighed.
In A, Reviewer_A5qv raised to 7 after the rebuttal; in B no score moved.
The one substantive caveat (SoS-versus-SQ) was raised in both; the one-committee-only issues were clarification requests that moved no score.
The notes record that the committees saw the same facts and weighted them the same way.
Neither chair resolved a split by adopting one reviewer's position; both panels were unanimous accepts.
No reviewer changed score because of other reviews; A5qv's raise cites the authors' arguments.
The authors did not understand 9Tob's thresholding question, but 9Tob kept an 8, so no score was lowered or held down.
Each committee has one thin 8 (8XsW, LQDD), so the feature is symmetric and does not separate the committees.
Both chairs accepted with a spotlight in line with all-accept ratings.
No chair decided by a score threshold against its own view; both accepted.
No reviewer kept a below-threshold score; all final ratings are 7 or 8.
Both committees read the paper as the same theory contribution, a lower bound matching the upper bounds.
The only reviewer moved by the rebuttal, A5qv, was at confidence 4 and engaged with the prior-work argument, not an out-of-expertise reviewer.
Neither committee required something extra of this kind of paper; both judged it by the same theory standard.
LQDD's 'information-theoretic' label is a summary slip noted as inattention; the notes do not tie its 8 to that claim, and A has a matching thin 8.
No reviewer held a below-threshold score after the main concern was answered; A5qv raised its score.
Both committees accepted with the promised SoS disclaimer; neither refused to credit promised revisions.
No reviewer's stated stance differed from the score; NeJG, twpW, iqKa and LQDD all stated continued support at their ratings.
No off-record extra reviewer appears in either committee.
Dense exposition was noted in both committees and penalised by neither; no expertise gap shaped a clarity verdict.
A5qv's raise came with a stated reason; no silent raise against the review text.
No low rating existed for a chair to set aside.
Both committees had reviewers at 8 backing the paper; neither lacked an advocate.
No reviewer admitted a partial reading at high confidence; NeJG said details were not carefully checked but rated at confidence 3 and raised no objection.
No reviewer contested the premise from another theoretical tradition.
Neither meta-review justified spotlight over poster, but both placed it in the same tier, so no tier gap rests on this.
Both committees knew the DKS17/DKS19 literature and judged the extension the same way.
A's meta-review cites a reviewer discussion not in the record, but it does not misstate final positions toward a lower decision; both accepted.
Neither committee raised a narrow-audience or venue objection.
Neither committee had a misreading low-scoring detractor; all ratings are 7 or 8.
The rebuttals added arguments and a formula for the reference variance, but no new results raised either committee's scores.
All reviewers in both committees rated at confidence 3 or 4 and 7 or 8; no expert was outweighed.
No late post-response objection exists in either committee.
Ratings (A 7, 8, 8, 8; B 7, 7, 8, 8) and verbal assessments match closely; no scale difference.
Both committees found the 'matches' claim limited by the SoS caveat and treated it as framing; neither capped the tier for it.
No committee converged on flat marginal-accept scores; both rated 7 and 8 at confidence 3 to 4.
